header_summary:
spscand version 1.1.2 introduces a watch-only scanner for BIP352 silent payments, prioritizing privacy by processing blockchain data locally and supporting multiple block sources, including Bitcoin Core RPC, BlindBit Oracle, and BIP158 filters. The underlying libspscan C library, which never accesses spend private keys and relies only on the standard C library and libsecp256k1, enables integration into wallets or indexers and ensures constant-time cryptographic operations and robust label matching, as detailed at the [spscand GitHub repository](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand). Comprehensive testing confirms privacy safeguards, correct filter operation, and practical resource usage ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/05fbac98-5a91-4224-ad9b-745441252e26n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#ma8201f1e47129be61257f5a0a3141cb879821f1e)).

Testnet5 is now operational with public libbitcoin nodes at wormer.libbitcoin.net:18353 and carmine.libbitcoin.net:18353, both supporting BIP54 and accessible to developers for peer connections. Node status and configuration details can be found at [libbitcoin public configuration](https://libbitcoin.org/configuration/public.html), while web explorers for testnet5 data are available at [wormer explorer](https://wormer.libbitcoin.net:58143) and [carmine explorer](https://carmine.libbitcoin.net:58143) ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/HY8DsUoVVHnLe80I6KVSNBpFNJpn8DI7Uf89FfWuKuKMAMAqJHDP5rmpPZi6zVp3JT2Px08Bncryhu05fxBioQ5_v2COC1r2LjncC6vNpFo=@pm.me/T/#u#m6fd1d1fb2dd1a81b7316378e77efec400601632c)).

A new transport layer upgrade negotiation mechanism for the P2P protocol proposes adopting ML-KEM-768 key establishment, balancing quantum resistance with efficiency and using payload structures and rekeying methods compatible with [FIPS 203](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/Events/2025/workshop-on-guidance-for-kems/documents/papers/kemeleon-paper.pdf). Nodes may optionally optimize bandwidth by skipping encapsulation key transmission until peer support is confirmed; feedback is invited on this and the parameter set choice ([BIP-324 details](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0324.mediawikielligatorswift-encoding-of-curve-x-coordinates), [source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/12a1a76d-0e27-4035-9fe8-a47524729c47n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m85f1ad08dcf59870a50431a82801279a866e9c93)).

A denial-of-service vulnerability affecting Core Lightning channel opening, tracked as [LNF-2026-0004](https://lnfuzz.org/advisories/cln-duplicate-funding-outpoint-dos/), has been resolved in [Core Lightning v26.06.8](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/releases/tag/v26.06.8). Users running versions v0.12.0 through v26.06.7 should upgrade promptly to mitigate risks of node crashes triggered by duplicate funding outpoints ([advisory and technical details](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/disclosure-dos-vulnerability-fixed-in-core-lightning-v26-06-8/3072)).

Recent protocol research advocates for validating UTXO set updates with per-block undo data commitments, as opposed to solely relying on block header validation, to enhance robustness and adaptability to future soft forks. This approach supports more efficient proof constructions and could benefit synchronization protocols like swiftsync, with further specifications proposed for accommodating both valid and invalid blocks ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-stark-proof-of-bitcoins-utxo-set-at-block-972-500-with-circuits-proven-in-lean/3070/3)).

A protocol-wide limit of 16 payout slots is recommended to standardize and simplify decentralized coinbase payout protocols, ensuring deterministic slot allocation and minimization of hardware dependency. This measure is expected to improve fairness and operational stability for all mining participants until future hardware advancements permit greater flexibility ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/decentralized-coinbase-payout-protocols-dcpp-a-framework-for-discussion/3060/8)).

recent_posts.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
recent_posts.summary: - spscand scans for BIP352 silent payments, supports multiple privacy-preserving block sources, and tracks blockchain reorganizations.  - The engine leverages libspscan for cryptographic operations, never exposes spend keys, and ensures constant-time computations.  - Comprehensive tests confirm reliable detection, privacy adherence, and compliance with BIP352 and BIP158 standards.

recent_posts.title: Testnet5 Launch
recent_posts.summary: - Two public libbitcoin nodes are connected to testnet5 and support direct peer connections.  - Node status, configuration, and connectivity data are provided online for monitoring purposes.  - Web explorers are available for easy blockchain navigation and inspection on the testnet.

recent_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
recent_posts.summary: - ML-KEM-768 is recommended for improved post-quantum security over ML-KEM-512 and ECDH.  - Payloads follow FIPS 203 standards, with selective encapsulation key sharing to optimize bandwidth usage.  - Rekeying occurs after ciphertext exchange, and invalid keys result in immediate disconnection.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerability fixed in Core Lightning v26.06.8
recent_posts.summary: - A denial-of-service flaw in Core Lightning allowed attackers to crash nodes using duplicate funding outpoints.  - The vulnerability impacted versions v0.12.0 through v26.06.7 and enabled persistent denial-of-service attacks.  - Users should urgently upgrade to the latest release to protect their nodes from these exploit scenarios.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Header validation employs proof of work, median time checks, and block version signaling for security.  - Commitments to per-block undo data, with UTXO set updates, strengthen block validation frameworks.  - Validating UTXO set updates improves efficiency, robustness, and adaptability compared to per-block mechanisms.

recent_posts.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
recent_posts.summary: - A fixed limit of sixteen payout slots standardizes and ensures predictability across all implementations.  - Deterministic slot allocation simplifies value-weighted draw schemes, increasing fairness and technical efficiency.  - Standardized allocation offers operational stability until future decentralization influences hardware limitations.

active_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
active_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format using ML-DSA-65 provides quantum resistance and enhanced security features.  - Backward compatibility is maintained via a soft fork, and a Python implementation is publicly available.  - Community feedback is requested on design, migration, and adoption before quantum threats become urgent.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal enables nodes to share stale block information to improve network observability.  - Technical specifications include BIP 434 `feature` messages, compressed headers, and limitations on tip age.  - This system can facilitate better diagnostics, efficient branch switching, and deeper insights into stale rates.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Transport Feature Negotiation
active_posts.summary: - The protocol enables structured negotiation of transport features like encryption and authentication in Bitcoin's network.  - Nodes exchange negotiation packets listing supported features and disconnect if headers are unrecognized.  - The system streamlines handshakes, ensures backward compatibility, and supports future feature expansions.

active_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
active_posts.summary: - Monitoring of Lightning gossip messages revealed reduced convergence delay and potential network inefficiencies.  - Channel_update and node_announcement message statistics highlight concerns about rate limits and message redundancy.  - Future plans include broadening data collection infrastructure and inviting community input on analysis and collaboration.

active_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts.summary: - Integrating Nested MuSig2 enables k-of-n multisig configurations, enhancing security and flexibility for Lightning nodes.  - Current Lightning Network limitations make seamless k-of-n multisig wallets challenging and may impact privacy or efficiency.  - Proposed BOLT protocol changes would replace shachain and introduce feature bits for better multisig compatibility.

active_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
active_posts.summary: - The draft proposes standardizing policy formats for co-signer transaction conditions, improving interoperability across wallets.  - It details different verification processes and ensures transparent, enforceable conditions for co-signing.  - Feedback is sought on data representation, blinded verification feasibility, attestation placement, expression language, and timelock needs.

today_in_history_posts.title: Relative txout amounts with a Merkleized Sum Tree and explicit miner fee.
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The proposal discusses secure partial spends of a single UTXO using tap branches and output amounts.  - It raises technical questions about implementation, potential benefits for privacy, and UTXO growth reduction.  - Drawbacks include restrictions on change address reuse and complexity with absolute spending amounts.

today_in_history_posts.title: Mitigating Channel Jamming with Reputation Credentials: a Protocol Sketch
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Credential tampering by intermediaries can cause credential wastage in classic payment paths.  - Routing nodes may unintentionally jam channels, but deliberate attacks are unlikely due to fee loss.  - Effective anti-jamming measures would mean most remaining jams are accidental failures.

today_in_history_posts.title: CTV, APO, CAT activity on signet
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- BIPs 118, 119, and 347 have introduced notable scripting enhancements, particularly on signet.
- APO and CTV enabled advanced transaction conditions and security mechanisms, with significant experimental applications.
- OP_CAT saw the highest transaction volume, mainly due to integration with Proof of Work faucet processes.
